turns.question: What refund authority model do you want for the support role: a bounded delegation with a hard amount threshold, mandatory refund reason capture, and an escalation path for exceptions? Recommended: permit support-initiated refunds up to a fixed limit per transaction with required reason entry, and require owner approval above that limit.

Should the delegated authority cover both full and partial refunds, with the same ceiling applied to the refunded amount rather than the original charge amount? Recommended: allow full or partial refunds within the delegated limit and route anything above it to owner approval.

contract.G: Delegate limited refund execution to support without granting unrestricted payment authority.
contract.T: Add support refund capability with bounded authority, required justification, and escalation for higher-risk refunds.
contract.S: Enable provider full and partial refund APIs for support up to $100 per transaction with mandatory reason capture; require owner approval above $100; include auditability and role changes needed for this path.
contract.V: Verify support can create full or partial refunds up to $100, larger refunds are blocked pending owner approval, refund reasons are required, and audit events record actor, amount, reason, and escalation outcome.
contract.X: Stop if approval routing, audit event design, or support-role permission boundaries cannot be specified from current product constraints.
contract.P: Persist until the authority boundary, refund modes, approval path, and audit expectations are explicitly documented for implementation.

promotions.name: Refund authority
promotions.evidence: Stable term introduced by the delegated-support decision: support may refund up to $100 with a required reason; amounts above that require an owner.

promotions.name: Delegated support refunds with threshold escalation
promotions.evidence: Consequential control decision: support moves from read-only billing access to execution authority for full or partial refunds up to $100, with owner approval above threshold and audit requirements added.

turns.question: What is the exact privacy boundary for 'local-only' processing: do file bytes, metadata, derived text, model prompts/completions, and telemetry payloads all need to remain device-resident with no remote egress? Recommended: define local-only as zero off-device transmission for source bytes, extracted metadata, derived text, model inputs/outputs, and telemetry content.

contract.G: Provide file processing that is strictly confined to the user's device.
contract.T: Replace current remote-text-processing behavior with an on-device-only pipeline and remove outbound telemetry content for this flow.
contract.S: Use the existing on-device parser for the primary format; prohibit transmission of file bytes, metadata, derived text, AI traffic, and telemetry excerpts off device for local-only mode.
contract.V: Verify no network path receives file content or derivatives, telemetry excludes payload excerpts for this feature path, and processing succeeds on-device for the primary format.
contract.X: Stop if any required file-processing or AI step still depends on remote services for the promised local-only mode.
contract.P: Persist until the privacy boundary is explicit enough to constrain architecture, telemetry, and verification.

promotions.name: Local-only processing
promotions.evidence: Stable term defined by the privacy boundary: file bytes, metadata, derived text, AI, and telemetry must all stay on device.

promotions.name: Zero-egress local processing mode
promotions.evidence: Consequential architectural decision: current remote AI-derived-text flow and telemetry excerpts are incompatible with the accepted local-only boundary and must be excluded or replaced on-device.

turns.question: What retention outcome should govern uploads relative to report lifecycle: should retention be keyed to upload age, report completion, or last dependent report completion, and what derived artifacts remain? Recommended: delete uploads on a fixed schedule after the last report that depends on them completes, while retaining non-source report summaries.

What user-facing recovery semantics do you want once an upload is deleted, given backups retain objects for 30 days: should deletion be treated as reversible during backup retention or as logically final with disaster-recovery exceptions only? Recommended: present deletion as final to users and treat backup copies as non-user-accessible disaster-recovery residue until they age out.

contract.G: Automatically remove stale customer uploads without breaking retained report history or misrepresenting deletion semantics.
contract.T: Define and implement an upload-retention policy tied to report completion and communicate final-deletion semantics despite backup lag.
contract.S: Delete uploads 90 days after their last report finishes; retain report summaries; do not offer user recovery after deletion even though disaster-recovery backups may still contain objects for up to 30 days.
contract.V: Verify retention jobs key off the last dependent report completion time, summaries remain accessible after upload deletion, deleted uploads are no longer user-recoverable, and user messaging states deletion is final.
contract.X: Stop if report-to-upload dependency tracking or deletion messaging cannot be specified well enough to enforce the chosen retention policy.
contract.P: Persist until retention trigger, preserved artifacts, and recovery semantics are explicit enough for implementation and compliance review.

promotions.name: Final deletion semantics
promotions.evidence: Stable term required by the backup mismatch: users are told deletion is final even though disaster-recovery backups age out later.

promotions.name: Upload retention keyed to last dependent report completion
promotions.evidence: Consequential policy decision: uploads are deleted 90 days after the last report finishes, report summaries are retained, and backups are treated as non-user-accessible residual copies for 30 days.
